newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Iranian leader blames U.S. for stoking Caspian row.
newsitem.headline: Iranian leader blames U.S. for stoking Caspian row.

text.p: The speaker of Iran's parliament on Saturday accused Washington of stoking a regional dispute over the status of the Caspian Sea and its offshore oil deposits, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
It quoted Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, now on an official visit to Russia, as accusing Washington of encouraging Azerbaijan to disagree with other states bordering the Caspian.

"The United States has a historical dream of establishing themselves in the Caspian Sea after they did this in the Gulf," Nateq-Nouri told Russian reporters. "The superpowers always use local factors to penetrate one region or another."
The row focuses over whether the Caspian is a sea or a lake. The issue ceased to be purely academic after huge offshore oil deposits were found there.
Russia has argued that the sea is a salt lake whose oil resources should be developed jointly by all five surrounding states -- Russia, Iran, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan.
Azerbaijan and, to a lesser extent, Kazakhstan argue that the Caspian is a sea, and each of the five should have its own separate share of the deposits.
Nateq-Nouri warned Azerbaijan, which has strained relations with Tehran, against giving the United States a chance of using disagreements among the Caspian states in its own interests.
Azerbaijan's president "is making a historic mistake by laying grounds for U.S. interference", Nateq-Nouri said. He did not mention Kazakhstan.
Iran faced a Western diplomatic backlash after a German court this week held its political leadership responsible for the 1992 murders of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Nateq-Nouri said Iran, Russia and Turkmenistan had similar views on the Caspian, and the three countries had tried hard but failed to reach a compromise with Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan.
"It is very difficult to reach a compromise because foreign intrigues are standing in our way," he said.
